questions.question: Aliko Dangote, used as an introductory example of entrepreneurship, started his small trading business at what age?
questions.explanation: Dangote started his small trading business as a young man of 21. Options B, A and C give other ages, but his story begins at 21, showing that entrepreneurship can start early with modest means.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote, who started a small trading business as a young man, came from which Nigerian state?
questions.explanation: Dangote is described as a young man from Kano State who began by trading. Options A, C and D are other Nigerian states that do not feature in his story.

questions.question: How did Aliko Dangote fund the small trading business he started at 21?

options.a: With a loan from his uncle
options.b: With savings from a salaried job
options.c: With a loan from a commercial bank
options.d: With a grant from the government

questions.explanation: Dangote started his trading business with a loan from his uncle, a good example of mobilising whatever resources are available. Options D, C and B sound like common ways to fund a business, but none of them is how his story began.

questions.question: Which goods did the young Aliko Dangote buy and sell in his early trading business?
questions.explanation: As a trader, Dangote bought and sold sugar, rice and cement, delivering the goods himself. Option C lists products his companies make today, not what he traded at the start, while B and D are not part of his story.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote noticed that Nigeria imported almost every product it consumed. What bigger opportunity did he see in this?

options.a: Export Nigerian raw produce to other countries
options.b: Import the same goods more cheaply than others
options.c: Open retail shops to sell imported goods
options.d: Produce locally what the country was importing

questions.explanation: Seeing that Nigeria imported almost everything it consumed, Dangote saw the bigger opportunity to produce locally what the country was importing. Options B and C would keep him dependent on imports, and A is about exporting raw produce, which is not the gap he spotted.

questions.question: When Aliko Dangote took the bold step from trading into manufacturing, which product did he start with?
questions.explanation: Dangote's bold step into manufacturing started with cement. Options B, D and A are products his companies make today, but they were not where his manufacturing journey began.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote's companies today produce several products. Which of the following is NOT one of the products listed for his companies?
questions.explanation: Dangote's companies produce cement, sugar, salt, pasta, fertilizer and petroleum products. Purified bottled water is the business of Tunde in a different case study, so C is the odd one out, while D, A and B are all on Dangote's list.

questions.question: What does the story of Aliko Dangote show about where entrepreneurship begins?

options.a: With copying successful foreign businesses without changes
options.b: With spotting opportunities, taking risks and creating value that meets national needs
options.c: With securing government contracts before starting any business
options.d: With inheriting a large family fortune and a ready market

questions.explanation: Dangote's journey shows that entrepreneurship begins with spotting opportunities, taking risks and creating value that meets national needs. He started small with a loan, so D is wrong, and his story says nothing about C or A.

questions.question: Besides producing goods, what wider impact are Aliko Dangote's companies described as having?

options.c: Replacing the need for small traders
options.d: Reducing the number of local manufacturers

questions.explanation: Dangote's companies are described as creating jobs and transforming industries. Option A is the opposite of his aim of producing locally, and D and C are not claims made about his companies.

questions.question: The process of identifying opportunities, mobilizing resources, creating innovative products or services and taking risks to generate value and achieve profit is called
questions.explanation: This is the definition of entrepreneurship: it brings together opportunities, resources, innovation and risk to generate value and profit. Options A and D are only single parts of that process (they appear as dimensions of entrepreneurship), and B is not defined this way.

questions.question: In the definition of entrepreneurship as a process, entrepreneurs identify opportunities, mobilize resources, create innovative products or services and take risks in order to

options.c: Copy existing products at lower cost

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship ends in generating value and achieving profit; that is the reason for taking on all the effort and risk. Options D, B and C are not part of the definition.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of the definition of entrepreneurship as the process of creating value and profit?

options.d: Delegating all risks to the government

questions.explanation: The definition includes identifying opportunities, mobilizing resources, creating innovative products or services and taking risks. Entrepreneurs take risks themselves, so D does not belong, while C, B and A are all in the definition.

questions.question: Apart from being a process of creating value and profit, entrepreneurship is also described as the mindset and process of

options.a: Avoiding risks, saving money and waiting for stability
options.b: Importing goods, reselling them and keeping the margin
options.c: Following instructions, meeting targets and earning wages
options.d: Discovering problems, designing innovative solutions and delivering value

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship as a mindset means discovering problems, designing innovative solutions and delivering value. Option A avoids risk, which entrepreneurs embrace, C describes an employee, and B is simple trading without innovation.

questions.question: When entrepreneurship is described as a mindset and process, to whom is value delivered?
questions.explanation: The mindset view says entrepreneurs deliver value to society, markets or organisations, which is a broad set of beneficiaries. Options C, B and A are too narrow because each limits value to only one small group.

questions.question: In simple terms, entrepreneurship can be expressed by which formula?
questions.explanation: The simple formula is Entrepreneurship = Opportunity + Innovation + Value Creation + Risk. Options B, C and A each swap in elements like capital, money, autonomy or profit that are not part of this formula.

questions.question: Complete the formula: Entrepreneurship = Opportunity + Innovation + ________ + Risk
questions.explanation: The missing element is Value Creation, giving Opportunity + Innovation + Value Creation + Risk. Option D is mentioned in the full definition but is not in the formula, and C and B are dimensions of entrepreneurship, not formula elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four elements in the simple formula for entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: The four elements are Opportunity, Innovation, Value Creation and Risk. Autonomy is one of the dimensions of entrepreneurship, not part of the formula, while A, D and C are all in it.

questions.question: Paystack and Flutterwave revolutionizing digital payments in Nigeria are examples of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Technological entrepreneurship is about tech-driven solutions, and Paystack and Flutterwave changed digital payments with technology. Option D happens inside large existing organisations, A is innovation in government agencies, and B relies on talent and culture.

questions.question: The scope of entrepreneurship described simply as 'tech-driven solutions' is
questions.explanation: Technological entrepreneurship is described as tech-driven solutions. Option A is about teaching and learning, D applies innovative ideas to farming for profit, and B involves activities across national borders.

questions.question: Leap Africa tackling youth development challenges is an example of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Social entrepreneurship means innovative solutions to social problems, and youth development is a social challenge. Option B takes place inside large firms, D crosses national borders, and C focuses on protecting the environment.

questions.question: Social entrepreneurship is best described as

options.a: Tech-driven solutions such as digital payments
options.b: Innovating within public agencies to improve service delivery
options.c: Innovative activities inside a large organisation
options.d: Innovative solutions to solving social problems

questions.explanation: Social entrepreneurship provides innovative solutions to social problems. Option A describes technological entrepreneurship, C is corporate entrepreneurship, and B is public sector entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Leap Africa, an example of social entrepreneurship, is known for tackling which challenge?
questions.explanation: Leap Africa tackles youth development challenges, which is why it illustrates social entrepreneurship. Option C matches Paystack and Flutterwave, B matches FarmCrowdy, and A matches the Sahara Energy Renewable Project.

questions.question: FarmCrowdy is an example of agricultural entrepreneurship because it

options.c: Runs a digital tax collection system

questions.explanation: FarmCrowdy uses crowdfunding for farming, bringing an innovative funding idea into agriculture. Option A relates to Dangote Cement, D sounds like educational entrepreneurship, and C is a public sector example.

questions.question: Agricultural entrepreneurship is described as

options.a: Creativity and cultural expressions to produce value
options.b: Innovative ideas to agriculture for profit

questions.explanation: Agricultural entrepreneurship brings innovative ideas to agriculture for profit. Option D describes green entrepreneurship, C is international entrepreneurship, and A is creative entrepreneurship.

questions.question: uLesson is given as an example of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: uLesson is the example of educational entrepreneurship, which is innovation in teaching, learning and educational services. Option C is illustrated by FarmCrowdy, D by Leap Africa, and A by online passport portals and digital tax systems.

questions.question: Educational entrepreneurship involves

options.b: Innovation in teaching, learning and educational services
options.c: Innovative solutions to youth development problems

questions.explanation: Educational entrepreneurship is innovation in teaching, learning and educational services. Option C describes social entrepreneurship such as Leap Africa, D is technological entrepreneurship, and A is corporate entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as an example of agricultural entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: FarmCrowdy uses crowdfunding for farming, making it the agricultural example. Option D is educational, C is social, and B is technological entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Nollywood films, music and fashion brands are examples of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Creative entrepreneurship uses creativity, talent and cultural expressions to produce value, which is exactly what Nollywood, music and fashion brands do. Option C happens inside large organisations, D is tech-driven, and B is innovation within government agencies.

questions.question: Creative entrepreneurship is described as using

options.c: Creativity, talent and cultural expressions to produce value
options.d: Crowdfunding and digital tools to support farmers

questions.explanation: Creative entrepreneurship turns creativity, talent and cultural expressions into value. Option D describes FarmCrowdy in agricultural entrepreneurship, A is international entrepreneurship, and B fits green entrepreneurship.

questions.question: MTN MoMo and Gmail at Google are examples of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Corporate entrepreneurship is innovation carried out inside large organisations to create new products, services or processes, as MTN did with MoMo and Google did with Gmail. Option B is about crossing borders, C solves social problems, and A relies on talent and culture.

questions.question: Innovative activities carried out inside a large organisation to create new products, services or processes are known as
questions.explanation: This is corporate entrepreneurship: innovation that happens inside a large existing organisation. Option C is innovation within government agencies, A involves activities across national borders, and B solves social problems.

questions.question: Entrepreneurial activities across national borders, such as exporting, expansion and foreign partnerships, are called
questions.explanation: International entrepreneurship covers activities across national borders, including exporting, expansion and foreign partnerships. Option D is innovation inside a large organisation, B is innovation in government agencies, and A protects the environment.

questions.question: Dangote Cement operating in 10 African countries illustrates which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: International entrepreneurship involves activities across national borders, and Dangote Cement operating in 10 African countries is the example. Option A is about innovation inside a large firm, like MTN MoMo, D happens in government agencies, and B solves social problems.

questions.question: As an example of international entrepreneurship, Dangote Cement is described as operating in how many African countries?
questions.explanation: Dangote Cement is said to operate in 10 African countries, showing entrepreneurship across national borders. Options A, C and B are not the number given in the example.

questions.question: Digital tax collection systems and online passport application portals are examples of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Public sector entrepreneurship means innovating within government agencies to improve service delivery, and digital tax collection and online passport portals are government services. Option B, creative entrepreneurship, uses creativity, talent and culture to produce value, as in Nollywood, music and fashion brands. Option A happens inside large private organisations, and D focuses on solving social problems.

questions.question: Public sector (government) entrepreneurship refers to

options.a: Innovative activities inside large private organisations
options.b: Innovating within public agencies to improve service delivery
options.c: Innovative solutions to solving social problems
options.d: Activities across national borders such as exporting

questions.explanation: Public sector entrepreneurship is about innovating within public agencies to improve service delivery. Option D describes international entrepreneurship, C is social entrepreneurship, and A is corporate entrepreneurship.

questions.question: The Sahara Energy Renewable Project is an example of which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Green or environmental entrepreneurship develops solutions that protect the environment or promote sustainability, and a renewable energy project does that. Option B is about operating across borders, C applies innovation to farming, and D uses talent and culture.

questions.question: Developing solutions that protect the environment or promote sustainability is known as
questions.explanation: This describes green or environmental entrepreneurship. Option D solves social problems, B brings innovative ideas to agriculture for profit, and C improves service delivery in government agencies.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of green/environmental entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Energy Renewable Project is the green entrepreneurship example because it promotes sustainability. Option D is corporate entrepreneurship, A is educational, and C is creative entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of public sector (government) entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Online passport application portals are innovation within government agencies to improve service delivery. Option D is corporate entrepreneurship, A is social, and B is agricultural.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of corporate entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Gmail was created inside Google, a large organisation, which makes it corporate entrepreneurship. Option C is social, B is green, and D is public sector entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the scopes of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Proactiveness is a dimension of entrepreneurship, describing how entrepreneurs act ahead of competitors; it is not a scope. Options B, C and D are all scopes of entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the scopes of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Agricultural entrepreneurship, bringing innovative ideas to farming for profit, is one of the scopes. Option D is a dimension of entrepreneurship, while A and B are characteristics of an entrepreneur.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Risk Taker is a characteristic of an entrepreneur, not a scope of entrepreneurship. Options A, D and C are all scopes.

questions.question: A state ministry in Nigeria introduces an online portal where residents can renew their driver's licences without visiting an office, improving service delivery. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Innovating within a public agency to improve service delivery is public sector entrepreneurship, just like online passport portals. Option A happens inside large private firms, B uses talent and culture, and D tackles social problems through ventures like Leap Africa.

questions.question: A team of staff inside a large Nigerian bank develops a brand-new mobile savings product for the bank's customers. This is best described as
questions.explanation: Innovation carried out inside a large organisation to create a new product is corporate entrepreneurship, like MTN MoMo or Gmail at Google. Option A would need a government agency, D would need activity across borders, and C focuses on social problems.

questions.question: A shoe maker in Aba begins exporting shoes to Ghana and forms a partnership with a distributor in Senegal. Which scope of entrepreneurship does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Exporting and forming foreign partnerships are activities across national borders, which is international entrepreneurship. Option B centres on talent and culture, C happens inside a large organisation, and D concerns farming.

questions.question: A young Lagos musician builds a profitable brand from her songs and performances that celebrate Yoruba culture. Which scope of entrepreneurship is this?
questions.explanation: Using talent and cultural expression to produce value is creative entrepreneurship, like Nollywood and music brands. Option C needs a large existing organisation, D needs a government agency, and A is about protecting the environment.

questions.question: An entrepreneur in Port Harcourt sets up a business that installs solar power systems to cut pollution from diesel generators and promote sustainability. This fits which scope of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: A business that protects the environment and promotes sustainability is green or environmental entrepreneurship, like the Sahara Energy Renewable Project. Option D uses talent and culture, B takes place inside a large organisation, and C involves activities across borders.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the characteristics of an entrepreneur?
questions.explanation: Autonomy is one of the dimensions of entrepreneurship, not one of the listed characteristics of an entrepreneur. Options D, B and A are all characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the characteristics of an entrepreneur?
questions.explanation: Ability to Network is one of the eight characteristics of an entrepreneur. Options B, D and C are dimensions of entrepreneurship rather than items on the list of characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of an entrepreneur?
questions.explanation: Technological is a scope of entrepreneurship, not a characteristic of the entrepreneur. Options B, A and C are all on the list of characteristics.

questions.question: Among the characteristics of an entrepreneur, 'Never Give-up' is also referred to as
questions.explanation: Never Give-up is shown as Grit, meaning the determination to keep going despite setbacks. Options A, B and C are separate characteristics on the same list.

questions.question: How many characteristics of an entrepreneur are listed (Vision, Creativity, Passion and so on)?
questions.explanation: There are eight characteristics: Vision, Creativity, Passion, Ability to Network, Self Confidence, Risk Taker, Resourceful and Never Give-up (Grit). Option A is the number of dimensions of entrepreneurship, which students often mix up with the characteristics.

questions.question: Kemi's catering business failed twice, but each time she learned from her mistakes and started again until the third attempt succeeded. Which characteristic of an entrepreneur does she show most clearly?
questions.explanation: Refusing to quit after repeated failure is Never Give-up, also called Grit. Option C is about building connections, D is about seeing the future clearly, and B is about new ideas, none of which is the main point of her story.

questions.question: Chidi attends business events, keeps in touch with mentors and builds relationships that later bring him partners and customers. Which characteristic of an entrepreneur is he showing?
questions.explanation: Building and using relationships with mentors, partners and customers is the Ability to Network. Option D is about making the most of limited resources, B is deep love for the work, and A is about taking chances, which are not what the scenario stresses.

questions.question: With very little money, Aisha starts a snack business using her mother's kitchen, second-hand utensils and free social media advertising. Which characteristic of an entrepreneur does this best show?
questions.explanation: Making the best use of the little she has is being Resourceful. Option C is about seeing the future, B is belief in oneself, and D is about relationships, none of which is the focus here.

questions.question: The dimensions of entrepreneurship describe the

options.a: Legal forms a business can take when it is registered
options.b: Behaviours, processes and characteristics that drive entrepreneurial activity
options.c: Sources of funds available to a new business
options.d: Sectors of the economy in which businesses operate

questions.explanation: The dimensions describe the behaviours, processes and characteristics that drive entrepreneurial activity. Option D is closer to the idea of scope, and A and C are not what the dimensions describe.

questions.question: How many dimensions of entrepreneurship are listed (Innovativeness, Proactiveness, Risk taking and so on)?
questions.explanation: There are seven dimensions: Innovativeness, Proactiveness, Risk taking, Value Creation, Opportunity Recognition, Resource Mobilisation and Autonomy. Option A is the number of characteristics of an entrepreneur and B is the number of scopes, which is why they can be confusing.

questions.question: Creating something new or improving existing products, services or processes is the dimension of entrepreneurship known as
questions.explanation: Innovativeness means creating something new or improving what already exists. Option C is acting ahead of competitors, D is creating economic, social or environmental value, and A is gathering and managing resources.

questions.question: Flutterwave creating an innovative payment infrastructure is used to illustrate which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Building a new payment infrastructure is creating something new, which is Innovativeness. Option A is about independence in decision-making, B is illustrated by Dangote investing despite uncertainty, and C is illustrated by Tony Elumelu and UBA.

questions.question: When entrepreneurs anticipate future trends, act ahead of competitors and seize opportunities early, they are displaying
questions.explanation: Anticipating trends and acting before competitors is Proactiveness. Option A is independence in decisions, B is creating something new or improving it, and C is taking calculated risks in uncertain environments.

questions.question: Sim Shagaya pioneering Konga online shopping is an example of which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: By pioneering e-commerce with Konga, Sim Shagaya acted ahead of competitors and seized the opportunity early, which is Proactiveness. Option C is about independent decision-making, B is illustrated by Tony Elumelu, and D is illustrated by FarmCrowdy.

questions.question: Which company did Sim Shagaya pioneer as an example of proactiveness?
questions.explanation: Sim Shagaya pioneered Konga, an e-commerce online shopping platform. Option A is a technological entrepreneurship example, C is educational, and D is agricultural.

questions.question: As a dimension of entrepreneurship, risk taking means that entrepreneurs

options.a: Take any risk without thinking in stable environments
options.b: Pass every risk on to their customers
options.c: Avoid all risks until success is guaranteed
options.d: Take calculated risks in uncertain environments

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs take calculated risks in uncertain environments, meaning they weigh the risks before acting. Option A describes reckless gambling, C would mean never starting at all, and B is not what risk taking means.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote investing in local industries despite import dominance and market uncertainty is the example given for which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Risk taking means entrepreneurs take calculated risks in uncertain environments, and investing despite import dominance and market uncertainty is exactly that. Option C, creativity, is listed as a characteristic of an entrepreneur rather than one of the dimensions. Option A is about independence in decision-making, and D is about creating something new or improving what exists.

questions.question: As a dimension of entrepreneurship, value creation can be
questions.explanation: Value creation covers economic, social or environmental value, so it is broader than profit alone. Option C is too narrow, and D and B are not the types of value named.

questions.question: FarmCrowdy connecting farmers with digital funding and agricultural support is used to illustrate which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: By linking farmers to funding and support, FarmCrowdy created value, so it illustrates Value Creation. Option A is about independence, C is illustrated by Sim Shagaya and Konga, and B is illustrated by Dangote.

questions.question: The dimension of entrepreneurship that begins with identifying unmet needs, market gaps or solutions to problems is
questions.explanation: Opportunity Recognition is where entrepreneurship begins: spotting unmet needs, market gaps or solutions to problems. Option A comes after, when resources are gathered, B is independence in decision-making, and D is taking calculated risks.

questions.question: Entrepreneurs knowing how to gather and manage the resources needed to bring ideas to life describes which dimension?
questions.explanation: Gathering and managing the resources needed to bring ideas to life is Resource Mobilisation. Option D is spotting the need in the first place, A is creating something new, and B is the value that results.

questions.question: Tony Elumelu turning UBA into a global bank is an example of which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Tony Elumelu is the example of Resource Mobilisation, the ability to gather and manage resources to bring ideas to life. Option A is about independence in decision-making, D is illustrated by Sim Shagaya and Konga, and C by Flutterwave.

questions.question: Independence in decision-making and control over one's goals and actions is the dimension of entrepreneurship called
questions.explanation: Autonomy means independence in decision-making and control over one's goals and actions. Option C is acting ahead of competitors, A is gathering and managing resources, and B is identifying unmet needs.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as the example of autonomy as a dimension of entrepreneurship?

options.b: Tony Elumelu turning UBA into a global bank

questions.explanation: Startup founders starting their own enterprises show autonomy, because they make their own decisions and control their goals. Option B illustrates Resource Mobilisation, A illustrates Proactiveness, and D illustrates Value Creation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the dimensions of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Passion is a characteristic of an entrepreneur, not a dimension of entrepreneurship. Options C, D and B are all dimensions.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the dimensions of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Opportunity Recognition is one of the seven dimensions of entrepreneurship. Options D, A and B are characteristics of an entrepreneur rather than dimensions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Social Entrepreneurship is a scope of entrepreneurship, not one of its dimensions. Options D, B and C are all dimensions.

questions.question: A Nigerian startup studies changing customer habits, predicts that cashless payments at roadside markets will soon be common, and launches a solution before any competitor. Which dimension of entrepreneurship is this?
questions.explanation: Anticipating a future trend and acting ahead of competitors is Proactiveness. Option C is independence in decision-making, A is gathering resources, and D is the value created, but the key feature here is moving early.

questions.question: Bola resigns from a salaried job to start her own firm because she wants to make her own decisions and control her goals. Which dimension of entrepreneurship does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Wanting independence in decision-making and control over one's goals is Autonomy. Option D is about acting ahead of competitors, A is about creating something new, and B is about the value delivered, none of which is her main motive.

questions.question: A UNILAG student notices that many students struggle to find affordable hostel accommodation near campus and sees this unmet need as a business gap. Which dimension of entrepreneurship is shown?
questions.explanation: Spotting an unmet need or market gap is Opportunity Recognition, the starting point of entrepreneurship. Option B would come later when the student gathers resources, C is about independence, and D is about taking calculated risks.

questions.question: In the reflection case, what opportunity did Tunde recognise in his neighbourhood?

options.a: People could not get cheap cement for building
options.b: People struggled to find clean, affordable drinking water
options.c: Students lacked access to online lessons
options.d: Farmers could not get funding for their farms

questions.explanation: Tunde noticed that people often struggled to find clean, affordable drinking water. Option A recalls Dangote's cement, C sounds like uLesson, and D sounds like FarmCrowdy, so none fits Tunde's story.

questions.question: What kind of business did Tunde start in the reflection case?

options.a: Selling water purification equipment to factories
options.d: Running a crowdfunding platform for farmers

questions.explanation: Tunde started a small business producing purified bottled water. Option C is how Dangote began, D describes FarmCrowdy, and A is not what Tunde did; he bought equipment for his own production.

questions.question: Why were the water options people relied on in Tunde's neighbourhood a problem?

options.a: Bottled water was free but hard to find
options.b: Local supplies were safe but far away
options.c: There was too much water and no storage
options.d: Bottled water was expensive and local supplies were unsafe

questions.explanation: People relied on bottled water, which was expensive, or on local water supplies that were unsafe. Options A, B and C each change the facts of the case.

questions.question: In the reflection case, which of the following was NOT one of the resources Tunde mobilised to start his business?
questions.explanation: Tunde rented a small space, bought equipment and hired staff. A loan from an uncle is part of Aliko Dangote's story, not Tunde's, so C is the one that does not belong.

questions.question: Tunde renting a small space, buying equipment and hiring staff best illustrates which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Gathering a space, equipment and staff to bring his idea to life is Resource Mobilisation. Option C is about independence in decisions, A is acting ahead of competitors, and B is creating something new, none of which these actions mainly show.

questions.question: Tunde noticing that his neighbours struggled to find clean, affordable drinking water is an example of which dimension of entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Spotting an unmet need, here clean and affordable water, is Opportunity Recognition. Option D came next when he rented space and bought equipment, B is about independence, and A is about taking calculated risks.

questions.question: To whom did Tunde market his purified bottled water?
questions.explanation: Tunde marketed his product to local shops and households in his area. Options C, A and B are not the customers named in the case.

questions.question: What happened to Tunde's business within a year?

options.a: It began exporting water to other countries
options.b: It made losses and he closed it down
options.c: It became profitable and he started expanding into nearby towns
options.d: It was bought by a large company

questions.explanation: Within a year, Tunde's business became profitable and he began expanding into nearby towns. Option B is the opposite of what happened, and D and A are not part of the case.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the learning objectives for the lesson on the concept of entrepreneurship?

options.a: Calculate the break-even point of a new venture
options.b: Understand the characteristics of an entrepreneur
options.c: Describe the scope and dimensions of entrepreneurship

questions.explanation: The lesson aims to help students define entrepreneurship, describe its scope and dimensions, and understand the characteristics of an entrepreneur and the dimensions of entrepreneurship. Calculating break-even is not one of these aims, while D, C and B are.

questions.question: In entrepreneurship, beyond simply starting a business, entrepreneurship is described as a mindset and a process of creating value by

options.a: securing loans, hiring staff, and expanding branches
options.b: copying proven ideas, cutting costs, and avoiding risk
options.c: winning contracts, lobbying, and controlling prices
options.d: identifying opportunities, taking risks, and innovating

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship is a mindset and a process of creating value through three things: identifying opportunities, taking risks, and innovating. Option A lists ordinary business activities, not the value-creating process itself. Option B is the opposite of the entrepreneurial mindset, which embraces calculated risk and new ideas.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four entrepreneurial traits?
questions.explanation: The four entrepreneurial traits are opportunity seeker, risk-taker, problem solver and change agent, so fund manager is the odd one out. Options A, B and C are all genuine members of the four traits, which is why they cannot be the answer to a NOT question.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the four entrepreneurial traits?
questions.explanation: Change agent is one of the four entrepreneurial traits, alongside opportunity seeker, risk-taker and problem solver. A change agent drives change, for example by building a solution instead of just complaining about a problem. Options B, C and D may sound businesslike, but none of them is one of the four traits.

questions.question: Which set correctly lists the four entrepreneurial traits?

options.a: Market follower, risk-taker, problem solver, change agent
options.b: Opportunity seeker, risk-taker, profit maximizer, change agent
options.c: Opportunity seeker, risk-taker, problem solver, change agent
options.d: Opportunity seeker, risk avoider, problem solver, change agent

questions.explanation: The four entrepreneurial traits are opportunity seeker, risk-taker, problem solver and change agent. Option D swaps in 'risk avoider', which contradicts the trait of taking calculated risks. Options A and B replace a genuine trait with 'profit maximizer' or 'market follower', which are not among the four.

questions.question: The ability to identify and capitalize on market gaps or unmet needs is the entrepreneurial trait known as
questions.explanation: An opportunity seeker identifies and capitalizes on market gaps or unmet needs. Option A is about taking risks after assessing downsides, not spotting gaps. Option B is about driving change by fixing problems, and option D is about thinking outside conventional frameworks.

questions.question: The opportunity seeker trait involves

options.a: risk assessment, tolerance for failure, and a high-reward mindset
options.c: market awareness, proactiveness, and visionary thinking
options.d: trade, negotiation, and supply chain management

questions.explanation: Opportunity seeking involves market awareness, proactiveness and visionary thinking, which together help an entrepreneur spot gaps and unmet needs. Option A describes the calculated risk-taker. Option B is how nurtured skills are developed, and option D is what Igba Boi apprentices are taught.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the elements involved in the opportunity seeker trait?
questions.explanation: Risk assessment belongs to the calculated risk-taker trait, which involves risk assessment, tolerance for failure and a high-risk, high-reward mindset. Options A, B and D are the three elements of the opportunity seeker: market awareness, proactiveness and visionary thinking.

questions.question: Proactiveness and visionary thinking are elements of which entrepreneurial trait?
questions.explanation: The opportunity seeker trait involves market awareness, proactiveness and visionary thinking. Option A involves risk assessment and tolerance for failure instead. Options B and C describe a solution-oriented mindset focused on fixing inefficiencies and driving change.

questions.question: Sim Shagaya is the founder of
questions.explanation: Sim Shagaya founded Konga, one of Nigeria's earliest e-commerce giants. Option A was founded by Olugbenga Agboola and Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, option C by Chinedu Azodoh, and option D by Jason Njoku.

questions.question: Sim Shagaya founding Konga is used to illustrate which entrepreneurial trait?

options.d: The problem solver and change agent

questions.explanation: Shagaya spotted a market gap, the need for a trusted online marketplace in Nigeria, which is what an opportunity seeker does. Option B is illustrated by Aliko Dangote's investments, and option D by DentistAtYourDoor and MAX.ng. Option C relates to the born-or-made debate and the Igba Boi system.

questions.question: Which two conditions in Nigeria did Sim Shagaya observe before founding Konga?

options.a: An infrastructure deficit and weak local manufacturing
options.b: Low penetration of formal retail and growing internet use
options.c: Widespread piracy and limited access to Nollywood films
options.d: Heavy Lagos traffic and poor dental care access

questions.explanation: Shagaya saw that formal retail had low penetration while internet use was growing, and that pointed him to the opportunity for a trusted online marketplace. Option D is the problem DentistAtYourDoor addressed, and option C is what iROKOtv tackled. Option A relates to Dangote's bet on local production.

questions.question: The opportunity Sim Shagaya identified in Nigeria, which led to Konga, was the need for
questions.explanation: Shagaya identified the opportunity for a trusted online marketplace, and Konga became one of Nigeria's earliest e-commerce giants. Option C describes DentistAtYourDoor, option D describes MAX.ng, and option A describes Flutterwave.

questions.question: Konga is described as

options.b: one of Nigeria's earliest e-commerce giants
options.c: a hub for arts, dining and theatre in Lagos
options.d: the first mobile dental clinic in Lagos

questions.explanation: Konga, founded by Sim Shagaya, is described as one of Nigeria's earliest e-commerce giants. Option D is DentistAtYourDoor, option A is the Igba Boi apprenticeship system, and option C is Terra Kulture.

questions.question: In entrepreneurship, opportunity-seeking is best described as

options.a: actively looking for frustrations and inefficiencies around you
options.b: waiting patiently for a sudden 'eureka' moment
options.c: inventing a completely new technology from scratch
options.d: avoiding uncertainty until success is guaranteed

questions.explanation: Opportunity-seeking means actively looking for frustrations and inefficiencies around you, not sitting back. Option B is exactly what it is said NOT to be. Option C is not required either, since Sim Shagaya did not invent e-commerce, and option D clashes with the idea that entrepreneurial risk is managed, not eliminated.

questions.question: Sim Shagaya did not invent e-commerce. What he did instead, as an opportunity seeker, was to

options.a: import a foreign e-commerce company without changes
options.b: build it only as an offline retail chain
options.c: apply it to the specific challenges and opportunities of the Nigerian market
options.d: wait for government to create the market first

questions.explanation: Shagaya took an existing idea, e-commerce, and applied it to the specific challenges and opportunities of the Nigerian market. This shows that opportunity seeking does not require inventing something new. Options A, B and D do not match this point about adapting an idea to a local market.

questions.question: Tolu notices that smartphone use is rising fast in her town while no local business sells groceries online. She sees this unmet need and launches an online grocery store before anyone else does. Which entrepreneurial trait does Tolu mainly show?
questions.explanation: Tolu identified and capitalized on a market gap, which defines the opportunity seeker, much like Sim Shagaya and Konga. Option B is about weighing downsides before taking risks, which the scenario does not emphasize. Option C refers to learned skills, and option A is about bouncing back from setbacks.

questions.question: The willingness to take calculated risks after assessing potential downsides describes
questions.explanation: The calculated risk-taker is willing to take risks, but only after assessing potential downsides. Option A is about identifying market gaps or unmet needs. Option D focuses on fixing inefficiencies, and option B is about thinking outside conventional frameworks.

questions.question: The calculated risk-taker trait involves

options.a: market awareness, proactiveness, and visionary thinking
options.b: high energy, natural charisma, and extraversion
options.d: risk assessment, tolerance for failure, and a high-risk, high-reward mindset

questions.explanation: Calculated risk-taking involves risk assessment, tolerance for failure and a high-risk, high-reward mindset. Option A lists the elements of the opportunity seeker. Option C lists learned skills, and option B mixes inborn qualities from the 'born' argument.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the elements involved in the calculated risk-taker trait?
questions.explanation: Visionary thinking is an element of the opportunity seeker, together with market awareness and proactiveness. Options B, C and D are the three elements of the calculated risk-taker.

questions.question: Tolerance for failure is an element of which entrepreneurial trait?
questions.explanation: The calculated risk-taker trait involves risk assessment, tolerance for failure and a high-risk, high-reward mindset. Option A involves market awareness, proactiveness and visionary thinking instead. Options B and C are about driving change and thinking outside conventional frameworks.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote's heavy investment in cement production and Oil & Gas is used to illustrate which entrepreneurial trait?

options.d: The problem solver and change agent

questions.explanation: Dangote invested heavily when others were skeptical, after understanding the infrastructure deficit, which is calculated risk-taking. Option C is illustrated by Sim Shagaya and Konga. Option D is illustrated by DentistAtYourDoor and MAX.ng, and option A by Terra Kulture, iROKOtv and Flutterwave.

questions.question: In which sectors did Aliko Dangote invest heavily when others were skeptical about local manufacturing capacity?
questions.explanation: Dangote invested heavily in cement production and Oil & Gas in Nigeria. Option A is the area of Konga, option D is Flutterwave's field, and option C is iROKOtv's field.

questions.question: When Aliko Dangote invested heavily in cement and Oil & Gas, what were others skeptical about?
questions.explanation: Dangote invested at a time when others doubted Nigeria's local manufacturing capacity, which is what made his move a real risk. Option B relates to Konga's market, option D to DentistAtYourDoor, and option A to iROKOtv.

questions.question: What made Aliko Dangote's risk a calculated one?

options.a: He understood Nigeria's infrastructure deficit and bet on the long-term need for local production
options.b: He had a guarantee that his investments could not fail
options.c: He waited until others had stopped being skeptical
options.d: He copied a business that had already succeeded in Nigeria

questions.explanation: Dangote's risk was calculated because he understood Nigeria's infrastructure deficit and bet on the long-term need for local production. Option B is wrong because entrepreneurial risk is about managing uncertainty, not eliminating it. Option C contradicts the fact that he invested while others were still skeptical.

questions.question: In entrepreneurship, entrepreneurial risk is about
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurial risk is about managing uncertainty, not eliminating it, as Dangote's calculated bet shows. Option D is the reverse of this idea. Option A ignores the 'calculated' part, since a calculated risk-taker assesses potential downsides first.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote's calculated risk in cement and Oil & Gas is said to have built

options.a: one of Nigeria's earliest e-commerce giants
options.d: the first mobile dental clinic in Lagos

questions.explanation: Dangote's calculated risk built a multi-billion-dollar industrial empire. Option A describes Konga, option D describes DentistAtYourDoor, and option C describes Flutterwave.

questions.question: Before putting most of her savings into a rice-processing mill, Ngozi studies what could go wrong, estimates possible losses and decides the long-term demand justifies the bet. She then invests heavily. Which trait does she show?
questions.explanation: Ngozi assessed the potential downsides before committing, which is the heart of the calculated risk-taker, similar to Dangote betting on long-term demand for local production. Option D would focus on spotting a market gap, which the scenario does not stress. Options A and B focus on driving change and generating unconventional ideas.

questions.question: What makes a risk 'calculated' in the calculated risk-taker trait?

options.a: It carries no chance of failure
options.b: It is taken only with borrowed money
options.c: It is taken after assessing potential downsides
options.d: It is approved by competitors first

questions.explanation: A calculated risk is one taken after assessing potential downsides. Option A is wrong because the trait involves tolerance for failure, so failure remains possible. Options B and D have nothing to do with how the trait is defined.

questions.question: A solution-oriented mindset focused on fixing inefficiencies and driving change, often creating social impact, describes

options.d: The problem solver and the change agent

questions.explanation: The problem solver and change agent has a solution-oriented mindset that fixes inefficiencies and drives change, often with social impact. Option C is about identifying market gaps or unmet needs. Option B is about taking risks after assessing downsides, and option A refers to inborn qualities.

questions.question: The problem solver and change agent mindset often results in
questions.explanation: The problem solver and change agent mindset fixes inefficiencies and drives change, often creating social impact. Option D describes the Igba Boi system. Options A and C are problems that other entrepreneurs responded to, not results of this mindset.

questions.question: Dr. Akintonwa Oluwayemisi is associated with which venture?
questions.explanation: Dr. Akintonwa Oluwayemisi launched DentistAtYourDoor, the first mobile dental clinic. Option C is Bolanle Austen-Peters' venture, option B is Chinedu Azodoh's, and option A is Sim Shagaya's.

questions.question: DentistAtYourDoor solved the problem of

options.b: dental care access in traffic-heavy Lagos

questions.explanation: DentistAtYourDoor solved the problem of dental care access in traffic-heavy Lagos by bringing the clinic to the people. Option C is the problem MAX.ng tackled, option A is iROKOtv's, and option D is Flutterwave's.

questions.question: How did Dr. Akintonwa Oluwayemisi solve the problem of dental care access in traffic-heavy Lagos?

options.a: By lobbying government to reduce traffic
options.b: By building the largest dental hospital in Lagos
options.c: By offering dental advice only on radio
options.d: By launching the first mobile dental clinic

questions.explanation: She launched the first mobile dental clinic, DentistAtYourDoor, which brings the service to the people instead of making them fight traffic. Options A, B and C do not describe what she did.

questions.question: Chinedu Azodoh is associated with
questions.explanation: Chinedu Azodoh is linked with MAX.ng, which created a tech-enabled, safer ride-hailing and delivery service. Option D is Jason Njoku's, option A belongs to Olugbenga Agboola and Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, and option C is Dr. Akintonwa Oluwayemisi's.

questions.question: MAX.ng solved the problem of

options.c: dental care access in traffic-heavy Lagos

questions.explanation: MAX.ng tackled unsafe, informal motorcycle taxis, popularly called okada, with a tech-enabled service. Option C is DentistAtYourDoor's problem, option A is the gap Konga addressed, and option D is what iROKOtv tackled.

questions.question: MAX.ng solved the okada problem by creating

options.a: a tech-enabled, safer, energy-saving and more reliable ride-hailing and delivery service
options.b: a trusted online marketplace for consumer goods
options.c: an online platform for Nollywood films
options.d: a payment infrastructure for global merchants

questions.explanation: MAX.ng created a tech-enabled, safer, energy-saving and more reliable ride-hailing and delivery service. Option B describes Konga, option C describes iROKOtv, and option D describes Flutterwave.

questions.question: DentistAtYourDoor and MAX.ng are both used to illustrate which entrepreneurial trait?

options.d: The problem solver and the change agent

questions.explanation: Both ventures fixed real, persistent problems, dental access in Lagos traffic and unsafe okada rides, which shows the problem solver and change agent. Option A is illustrated by Sim Shagaya, option B by Aliko Dangote, and option C by the Igba Boi system.

questions.question: In entrepreneurship, the most sustainable businesses are those that
questions.explanation: The most sustainable businesses solve a persistent problem, like DentistAtYourDoor did with dental access in Lagos traffic. Option D is not presented as the key to sustainability. Option A contradicts calculated risk-taking, and option B ignores the role of learned skills.

questions.question: Dr. Oluwayemisi did not just complain about the traffic in Lagos; she built a mobile clinic to bring the service to the people. This is described as being
questions.explanation: Turning a complaint into action that brings a service to people is what being a change agent means. Option A focuses on taking risks after assessing downsides. Option C refers to the apprenticeship system, and option B refers to inborn traits, none of which this example is used to show.

questions.question: In Yaba, students waste hours queuing for water at one borehole. Emeka builds a cheap tech-enabled booking and delivery system that ends the queues and improves life in the area. Which trait does this best show?
questions.explanation: Emeka fixed an inefficiency and drove change with social impact, which is the problem solver and change agent mindset. Option C would stress weighing potential downsides before a big bet. Options A and D relate to the born-or-made debate rather than to a trait shown in action.

questions.question: Complete the statement: 'Entrepreneurs thrive on ...'
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs thrive on solving real problems, which is why the most sustainable businesses solve persistent ones. Option C is rejected because opportunity-seeking means actively looking for frustrations. Option A is wrong because entrepreneurial risk manages uncertainty rather than eliminating it.

questions.question: The 'Natural Traits (Born)' argument holds that some people have, from birth,

options.a: high energy, natural charisma, and high risk tolerance
options.d: trade, negotiation, and supply chain knowledge

questions.explanation: The born argument says some people have high energy, natural charisma and high risk tolerance from birth. Option C lists learned skills from the 'made' argument. Option D is what Igba Boi apprentices are taught, and option B involves mentorship, which is nurture.

questions.question: The 'Nurtured Traits (Made)' argument holds that entrepreneurial skills are developed through
questions.explanation: The made argument says skills are developed through education, mentorship and experience. Option C lists qualities from the born argument. Options B and D are not given as ways entrepreneurial skills are built.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a learned skill in the 'made' argument?
questions.explanation: Accounting, management, marketing and emotional intelligence are listed as learned skills. Options B, C and D come from the born argument, which points to qualities people have from birth or that appear early.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the learned skills in the 'Nurtured Traits (Made)' argument?
questions.explanation: Natural charisma belongs to the born argument, along with high energy and high risk tolerance from birth. Options B, C and D are all named as learned skills, together with management.

questions.question: In the 'born' argument, which of the following is named as an inherent quality that appears early in some people?
questions.explanation: The born argument names resilience, creativity and extraversion as inherent qualities that appear early for some people. Options B and D are learned skills, and option A is something Igba Boi apprentices are taught.

questions.question: Igba Boi is another name for
questions.explanation: Igba Boi is the Igbo Apprenticeship System, in which young people are mentored and then 'settled' to start their own businesses. Options A, B and D have no link to the term.

questions.question: The 'world's largest business incubator', found right here in Nigeria, refers to
questions.explanation: The Igbo Apprenticeship System, Igba Boi, is called the world's largest business incubator. Option C is an e-commerce company, option D is a cultural hub and option B is a payment company.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the Igba Boi process?

options.b: Picked, then nurtured through years of mentorship, then settled (funded)

questions.explanation: Young people are first picked, often with no capital, then nurtured through years of mentorship, and finally settled, meaning funded to start their own business. Options A, C and D put the steps out of order, for example funding before the mentorship has happened.

questions.question: In the Igba Boi system, being 'settled' means the apprentice is

options.b: funded to start his own business

questions.explanation: Being settled means the apprentice is funded to start his own business after years of mentorship. Options A, C and D contradict the idea that the system ends with a new, independent business.

questions.question: Young people picked into the Igba Boi system often start with

options.b: an established shop of their own

questions.explanation: Apprentices are often picked with no capital, and the system later funds them when they are settled. Options B, C and D miss the point that the system builds entrepreneurs from scratch.

questions.question: The Igba Boi system is said to have a success rate of
questions.explanation: The Igba Boi system is said to have a near 100% success rate, which is used as proof that entrepreneurs can be made. Options A, B and C understate this figure.

questions.question: The Igba Boi system is presented as the perfect example of

options.a: nature, proving that entrepreneurs are born
options.b: inheritance, proving wealth passes in families
options.d: nurture, proving that entrepreneurs can be made

questions.explanation: Igba Boi is the perfect example of nurture: young people are taught and mentored, which proves entrepreneurs can be made. Option A is the opposite conclusion. Options B and C are not ideas linked to the system.

questions.question: Igba Boi apprentices are taught

options.a: market awareness, proactiveness, and visionary thinking
options.b: risk assessment and tolerance for failure only
options.d: trade, negotiation, and supply chain management

questions.explanation: Apprentices are taught trade, negotiation and supply chain management, which is why they come to know things like the price of spare parts. Option C mixes learned skills with charisma, which is inborn. Option A lists opportunity seeker elements, and option B describes the risk-taker.

questions.question: The remark 'These boys aren't born knowing the price of spare parts' supports which view?

options.a: Entrepreneurs are only born with natural traits
options.c: Entrepreneurs can be made through nurture

questions.explanation: The point is that apprentices learn trade knowledge such as prices through mentorship, so entrepreneurs can be made. Option A is the view this remark argues against. Options B and D are contradicted by apprentices starting with no capital and being taught their skills.

questions.question: At 14, Chuka leaves his village to serve a spare-parts dealer in Onitsha with no money of his own. After seven years of learning the trade, his master gives him funds to open his own shop. Which concept does this describe?
questions.explanation: Being picked with no capital, mentored for years and then settled with funds is exactly the Igba Boi process. Option C argues that traits are inborn, which this story contradicts. Options A and B relate to risk, not to an apprenticeship model.

questions.question: In the entrepreneurial self-assessment profile, 'How do you bounce back from setbacks?' measures
questions.explanation: Resilience is about how you bounce back from setbacks. Option B asks about comfort with calculated, uncertain outcomes, option D about generating new ideas, and option C about spotting problems or gaps.

questions.question: In the entrepreneurial self-assessment profile, 'How comfortable are you with calculated, uncertain outcomes?' measures
questions.explanation: Risk Tolerance asks how comfortable you are with calculated, uncertain outcomes. Option D is about bouncing back from setbacks, option B about moving from a problem to solutions, and option A about generating new ideas.

questions.question: In the entrepreneurial self-assessment profile, 'How quickly do you move from identifying a problem to brainstorming solutions?' measures
questions.explanation: Problem-Solving measures how quickly you move from identifying a problem to brainstorming solutions. Option C is tempting, but it asks how often you spot problems or gaps, not how fast you turn to solutions. Options B and D are about uncertain outcomes and bouncing back.

questions.question: In the entrepreneurial self-assessment profile, the Opportunity Seeking dimension asks

options.a: How do you bounce back from setbacks?
options.b: How comfortable are you with calculated, uncertain outcomes?
options.c: How often do you spot problems or gaps around you?
options.d: How easily do you generate new ideas or unconventional approaches?

questions.explanation: Opportunity Seeking asks how often you spot problems or gaps around you. Option D is the Creativity question, option A is Resilience, and option B is Risk Tolerance.

questions.question: In the entrepreneurial self-assessment profile, the Creativity dimension asks

options.a: How often do you spot problems or gaps around you?
options.b: How do you bounce back from setbacks?
options.c: How quickly do you move from identifying a problem to brainstorming solutions?
options.d: How easily do you generate new ideas or unconventional approaches?

questions.explanation: Creativity asks how easily you generate new ideas or unconventional approaches. Option A is Opportunity Seeking, option C is Problem-Solving, and option B is Resilience.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the labelled dimensions in the 'Assess Your Entrepreneurial Profile' self-assessment?
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence appears as a learned skill in the born-or-made debate, not as a self-assessment dimension. Options A, C and D are labelled dimensions, together with Problem-Solving and Creativity.

questions.question: Introducing new products, services, or business models is called
questions.explanation: Innovation introduces new products, services or business models; it turns an idea into reality. Option B is thinking outside conventional frameworks to develop unique solutions, which is the idea stage. Options A and C are entrepreneurial traits or profile dimensions, not this definition.

questions.question: Thinking outside conventional frameworks to develop unique solutions is called
questions.explanation: Creativity is thinking outside conventional frameworks to develop unique solutions. Option B is the act of introducing new products, services or business models, which makes ideas real. Option C is an element of opportunity seeking, and option D is about bouncing back from setbacks.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes creativity from innovation?

options.a: Creativity and innovation both mean introducing new business models
options.b: Creativity is learned, while innovation is inborn
options.c: Creativity involves having a better idea; innovation involves making it a reality
options.d: Innovation involves having a better idea; creativity involves making it a reality

questions.explanation: Creativity is having a better idea, while innovation is making that idea a reality. Option D swaps the two, which is a common trap. Option A wrongly treats them as the same, and option B is not how the two are distinguished.

questions.question: Bisi sketches a clever new design for a solar-powered phone charger in her notebook. Months later, Kunle manufactures and sells it to customers in Ibadan. Bisi's sketch and Kunle's launch represent, respectively,
questions.explanation: Bisi had the better idea, which is creativity, and Kunle made it a reality as a product on the market, which is innovation. Option C reverses the pair. Options B and D do not describe the move from idea to product.

questions.question: Bolanle Austen-Peters is associated with
questions.explanation: Bolanle Austen-Peters is behind Terra Kulture, which reimagined the cultural space in Lagos. Option D is Jason Njoku's, option A is Sim Shagaya's, and option B is Dr. Akintonwa Oluwayemisi's.

questions.question: Terra Kulture is described as having

options.a: launched the first mobile dental clinic in Lagos
options.b: reimagined the cultural space in Lagos, creating a vibrant hub for arts, dining, and theatre
options.c: revolutionized Nollywood content distribution by moving it online
options.d: provided payment infrastructure for merchants across Africa

questions.explanation: Terra Kulture reimagined the cultural space in Lagos as a vibrant hub for arts, dining and theatre. Option C describes iROKOtv, option D describes Flutterwave, and option A describes DentistAtYourDoor.

questions.question: Jason Njoku is associated with
questions.explanation: Jason Njoku is linked with iROKOtv, which moved Nollywood content distribution online. Option C is Chinedu Azodoh's, option D belongs to Olugbenga Agboola and Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, and option B is Bolanle Austen-Peters'.

questions.question: iROKOtv revolutionized Nollywood content distribution by moving it online. Which issues did this solve?
questions.explanation: Moving Nollywood distribution online helped solve piracy and access issues. Option D relates to DentistAtYourDoor, option A to MAX.ng, and option C to Flutterwave.

questions.question: Flutterwave is associated with
questions.explanation: Flutterwave is linked with Olugbenga Agboola and Iyinoluwa Aboyeji. The pairs in options C, A and D are entrepreneurs linked with other ventures, such as iROKOtv, MAX.ng, Konga, Dangote's industries, Terra Kulture and DentistAtYourDoor.

questions.question: Flutterwave solved the payment challenge in Africa by

options.a: providing a payment infrastructure for global merchants and payment service providers across the continent
options.b: moving Nollywood films online to fight piracy
options.c: creating a hub for arts, dining and theatre
options.d: building a trusted online marketplace for Nigerian shoppers

questions.explanation: Flutterwave provides a payment infrastructure for global merchants and payment service providers across Africa. Option D describes Konga, option B describes iROKOtv, and option C describes Terra Kulture.

questions.question: Terra Kulture, iROKOtv and Flutterwave are all used as examples of
questions.explanation: These three ventures introduced new services or business models, so they are examples of innovators and creative thinkers. Option B is illustrated by Aliko Dangote. Options C and D come from the born-or-made debate.

questions.question: Which entrepreneur is cited as an example of innovators and creative thinkers?
questions.explanation: Jason Njoku of iROKOtv is an example of innovators and creative thinkers for moving Nollywood distribution online. Option A illustrates the opportunity seeker, option C the calculated risk-taker, and option B the problem solver and change agent.

questions.question: The systematic practice of developing and marketing breakthrough products and services for adoption by customers is known as
questions.explanation: Innovation is the systematic practice of developing and marketing breakthrough products and services so that customers adopt them. Option B (invention) is only coming up with something new, not making it work in the market. Options A and D deal with managing knowledge and managing change, not with bringing breakthrough offerings to customers.

questions.question: The definition of innovation as "the systematic practice of developing and marketing breakthrough products and services for adoption by customers" is attributed to
questions.explanation: This definition of innovation comes from McKinsey (2022). Option D, Kurt Lewin, is linked to the 3-stage model of planned change, not to this innovation definition. Options A and B are not where this particular definition comes from.

questions.question: In entrepreneurship, innovation is best described as

options.a: The habit of preferring familiar ways of doing things
options.b: The process of managing an organisation's stored information
options.c: The mere invention of a new idea or device
options.d: The successful implementation of new ideas that create value

questions.explanation: Innovation means successfully implementing new ideas that create value, so an idea has to work in the real world. Option C is tempting, but innovation is not just invention. Option B describes knowledge management, and option A describes resistance to change.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the difference between innovation and invention?

options.a: Invention creates value while innovation only generates ideas
options.b: Innovation is about making an idea work in the real world, not just inventing it
options.c: Innovation and invention mean exactly the same thing
options.d: Invention is the marketing of an idea while innovation is its design

questions.explanation: Innovation goes beyond invention: it is about making an idea work in the real world so that it creates value. Option A reverses the relationship, and option C ignores the clear point that innovation is not just invention. Option D invents a distinction that has nothing to do with value creation.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the four dimensions of innovation?
questions.explanation: The four dimensions of innovation are product, process, market and organisational innovation, so organisational innovation is a correct member. Options A, B and D sound reasonable but are not among the four dimensions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four dimensions of innovation?
questions.explanation: Refreeze is the final stage of Kurt Lewin's change model, not a dimension of innovation. Options A, B and D are all genuine dimensions, alongside organisational innovation.

questions.question: How many dimensions of innovation are identified?
questions.explanation: Innovation has four dimensions: product, process, market and organisational. Option A (three) is the number of stages in Kurt Lewin's change model, which is easy to confuse. Options B and D do not match the four listed dimensions.

questions.question: Product innovation is mainly concerned with

options.a: Who you sell to and how you reach them
options.d: How you structure and manage your company

questions.explanation: Product innovation focuses on what you sell, that is, the product or service itself. Option C describes process innovation, option A describes market innovation, and option D describes organisational innovation.

questions.question: The dimension of innovation summed up as "How you create it" is
questions.explanation: Process innovation is about how you create a product or deliver it. Option A is about what you sell, option D is about who you sell to and how you reach them, and option B is about how the company is structured and managed.

questions.question: "Who you sell to and how you reach them" describes which dimension of innovation?
questions.explanation: Market innovation is about who you sell to and how you reach them, such as finding new target customers or new packaging. Option A is about how the product is created, option D is about what is sold, and option C is about company structure and management.

questions.question: "How you structure and manage your company" refers to
questions.explanation: Organisational innovation concerns how a company is structured and managed, including its workplace culture. Option B is about customers and reach, option A is about how products are made or delivered, and option D is about what is sold.

questions.question: Product innovation involves

options.a: Improving a product or creating a totally new one
options.b: Finding new markets or packaging for existing products
options.d: Changing how a product is created or delivered to lower cost

questions.explanation: Product innovation means improving an existing product or creating a totally new one. Option D is process innovation, option B is market innovation, and option C is organisational innovation.

questions.question: Process innovation is defined as

options.a: Finding new markets or packaging for existing products
options.b: Changing how a product is created or delivered to lower cost or increase speed
options.d: Improving a product or creating a totally new one

questions.explanation: Process innovation changes how a product is created or delivered, with the aim of lowering cost or increasing speed. Option D is product innovation, option A is market innovation, and option C is organisational innovation.

questions.question: Finding new markets or packaging for existing products is called
questions.explanation: Market innovation means finding new markets or new packaging for products that already exist, which is why it is linked to new targets. Option C changes the product itself, option B changes how it is made or delivered, and option A changes the company's culture or structure.

questions.question: Changing workplace culture or structure is an example of
questions.explanation: Organisational innovation, also described as new structures, involves changing workplace culture or structure. Option D is about production and delivery methods, option B is about new markets or packaging, and option C is about the product itself.

questions.question: Market innovation is also described by which label?
questions.explanation: Market innovation is labelled "New Targets" because it is about reaching new customers or markets. Option D, "New Structures", is the label for organisational innovation. Options B and C are not labels used for market innovation.

questions.question: Organisational innovation is also described by which label?
questions.explanation: Organisational innovation is labelled "New Structures" since it changes workplace culture or structure. Option B, "New Targets", belongs to market innovation, and options A and D are also features of market innovation, not organisational innovation.

questions.question: Cowrywise and Piggyvest taking the traditional wooden Kolo (savings box) and moving it to an app with interest rates is an example of
questions.explanation: Cowrywise and Piggyvest improved the savings product itself, turning the wooden Kolo into an app that pays interest, which is product innovation. Option C would be about delivery logistics, option D about new markets or packaging, and option A about workplace culture.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as an example of product innovation?

options.d: The sachet economy for Peak Milk

questions.explanation: Cowrywise and Piggyvest are the product innovation example because they turned the Kolo savings box into an interest-paying app. Option A illustrates process innovation, option D illustrates market innovation, and option B illustrates organisational innovation.

questions.question: In the product innovation example, what traditional item did Cowrywise and Piggyvest move to an app?

options.c: The big tin of Peak Milk

questions.explanation: Cowrywise and Piggyvest took the traditional wooden Kolo, a savings box, and moved it to an app with interest rates. Option C belongs to the sachet economy example, while options A and B come from the change examples about gas cylinders and the Lagos Okada ban.

questions.question: Chowdeck and Glovo using bikes and bicycles to deliver within 30 minutes in Lagos traffic illustrates
questions.explanation: The innovation by Chowdeck and Glovo is the logistics process of delivering with bikes and bicycles to beat Lagos traffic, which is process innovation. Option C is tempting because food delivery is a service, but the new thing here is how it is delivered, not what is sold. Options B and D deal with new markets and workplace structure.

questions.question: In the Chowdeck and Glovo example, the logistics process using bikes/bicycles allowed delivery in Lagos traffic within
questions.explanation: The bike and bicycle logistics process allowed Chowdeck and Glovo to deliver within 30 minutes despite Lagos traffic. Options A, B and C are not the time stated for this example.

questions.question: For Chowdeck and Glovo, what exactly was the innovation?

options.a: Allowing staff to work from home
options.b: Selling food in smaller sachets to low-income earners
options.c: Creating a totally new type of food
options.d: The logistics process of using bikes/bicycles to beat Lagos traffic

questions.explanation: The innovation was the logistics process: using bikes and bicycles so deliveries could get through Lagos traffic quickly. Option C would be product innovation, option B resembles the sachet economy (market innovation), and option A resembles the Andela example (organisational innovation).

questions.question: Companies selling Peak Milk in sachets because most Nigerians cannot buy big tins is an example of
questions.explanation: The sachet economy is market innovation because the milk stayed the same, but new packaging opened a massive market of low-income earners. Option D is tempting, yet the product itself was not changed. Option B concerns how products are made or delivered, and option C concerns workplace culture.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as an example of market innovation?
questions.explanation: The sachet economy is the market innovation example, where packaging Peak Milk in sachets opened a market for low-income earners. Option C is product innovation, option D is process innovation, and option A is organisational innovation.

questions.question: In the sachet economy example, innovating the packaging opened a massive market for which group?
questions.explanation: Most Nigerians could not buy big tins of Peak Milk, so sachet packaging opened a massive market for low-income earners. Options A, B and C are not the group this packaging change reached.

questions.question: Andela and other tech startups moving from the "Oga must see you at your desk" mentality to a results-based culture where staff can work from home illustrates
questions.explanation: Shifting from desk-watching to a results-based, work-from-home culture is a change in workplace culture and structure, which is organisational innovation.
